title: Karmic tail 6 5 17 in the destiny matrix: desire, dogma and an ideal around one choice

seo.title: 6 5 17 in the destiny matrix: the karmic tail M–N–D
seo.description: The 6-5-17 tail in the destiny matrix: The Lovers, The Hierophant and The Star in the strict order M–N–D, with the formula and a practical reading.

short: The karmic tail 6-5-17 is not about three separate themes but about one choice that is stuck. The Lovers pull towards a living person and a living cause, The Hierophant holds the learned rule of “how it should be done”, and The Star shines with the picture of “how it ought to be”. The living “I want” is always there — but on its way to “yes” both the rule and the dream reject it, while the dream keeps pushing the moment further off. The trio is about desire spinning its wheels between dogma and an ideal, and about the place where it starts moving again.

sections.h2: A living desire and its two judges
paragraphs: Taken one by one, these arcana are about different things. The sixth, The Lovers, lives on response: its energy lights up when there is a “yes” coming back — a person, a cause, a place that genuinely pulls. The fifth, The Hierophant, carries inside a code of “how it is done properly”: a footing in tradition, order, a tested pattern. The seventeenth, The Star, keeps a clear picture of the future in mind and measures everything around by it. In a karmic tail, though, they do not stand apart — all three fall upon the same thing at once: the choice. With whom, with what, where to. And that is where their shared story begins.

A karmic tail is a repeating script inherited through the family line; it keeps turning on its own until it is lived through consciously, and the general page covers that at length. What matters here is something else: the meaning of 6-5-17 lives not in each arcanum separately but in the way they catch on one another. Attraction calls towards what is alive, the rule demands what is “proper”, the ideal demands what is “perfect” — and the living desire ends up not as the owner of the choice but as a defendant before two judges at once.

The machinery of this trio is simple, and that is why it is so stubborn. First attraction flares up — towards a person, a cause, a turn in life. That is the six: alive, warm, with somebody’s face on it. Almost at once a double check switches on. The Hierophant asks: “is this really how it should be, is this the proper choice?” The Star asks: “does it come up to the way I pictured it?” A living person or a living option almost never passes both checks at the same time: it is rarely both “right by the rules” and “perfect by the picture”.

The result is not an honest “no” but a sticky “maybe, just not now”. The choice is postponed, and the person stays open to everyone at once so as not to make a mistake (the weak side of the six), while the dream quietly defeats every concrete step (the weak side of The Star). The nastiest part is that each new round starts with less trust in your own attraction: if my “I want” has been rejected so many times, is it worth listening to at all. So the living desire slowly falls silent, and the decision is still passed by two parties to whom that desire is foreign.

sections.h2: The Star: an ideal that the living always loses to
paragraphs: The light of The Star comes from “not yet here” — it is a promise and a direction, not what exists right now. As long as the picture of the future works as a lighthouse, it leads and gives meaning. The trouble starts when it is used as a yardstick for rejecting the living: the more perfect the image, the more a real person or a real option looks like a spoiled version of it. Whoever is beside you always turns out to be slightly “not the one” — not because they are bad, but because they are compared not with other living people but with a picture that does not exist yet and may never exist.

This is where The Star strikes right at the strength of the six. The point of The Lovers is to arrive not first but together, with a companion. The ideal, though, slips in the image of a companion instead of a companion, and the living person loses to the imagined one time after time. The longer the checking goes on, the further off the moment of choice is pushed: the ideal does not come closer for it — it moves away, and the one who was ready to walk beside you leaves with it.

sections.h2: The Hierophant: whose “how it should be” is this
paragraphs: The five brings a rule into the trio: about the “right” person, the “right” path, the “right” order and the age at which each thing is due. The Hierophant leans on tradition and authority — that is its strength, and that is also its trap. The main conflict of the five is between your own voice and someone else’s authority, and in a karmic tail it easily swaps the personal “I want” for a learned “this is how it is done”: from the family line, from your surroundings, from “everyone does it this way”. The rule may not be one you earned through your own experience but simply one you picked up — and it still tries the living attraction as the highest court.

One question to the rule unglues the whole knot: whose rule is it, and what happens if it turns out not to be mine. The Hierophant is no enemy — it gives footing, and without footing a choice turns into chaos. What does harm is not the footing itself but its role as supreme judge: when a learned dogma gets a veto over who and what genuinely pulls you. Give the rule back the status of one voice among several rather than a sentence, and desire gets a chance to be heard.

sections.h2: Where the choice starts moving again
paragraphs: You do not get out of this by cancelling the rule or giving up the dream — both the footing and the landmark stay your strength. The way out is to give the living desire a vote before it is handed over for trial. Four habits hit exactly the joint between these three arcana, rather than each of them separately.

Name the “I want” before the checking starts. While the attraction has not been spoken out in its own right, the rule and the ideal intercept it before it takes shape. Honesty first: who and what actually pulls me — and only then everything else.

Ask the rule about its authorship. Check every “this is how it must be”: is it mine, earned through my own experience, or picked up from someone else. What was picked up can stay as one voice among others, but not as a final sentence on a living choice.

Translate the ideal into one real step. Do not measure a living person against the whole picture; take one feature out of the image that can be tested in life right now, and make a step towards the imperfect. A strong Star is the one that turns a design into at least one real action.

Decide, and stand by what you decided. The strength of the six is not in staying open to everyone at once but in choosing one particular person and keeping the connection. Choosing the imperfect is not the defeat of the dream but its landing in real life. The circle holds because the living “I want” is never accepted as enough; it comes undone where desire gets its voice back before the rule and the ideal give their verdict.

faq.a: The order makes them two different sequences. This page covers only 6-5-17: 6 The Lovers takes the entry position M, 5 The Hierophant the holding position N, and 17 The Star the root position D. Rearranging them changes the roles, so it cannot count as another spelling of the same tail.

faq.q: How does the formula produce the middle number 5 in the tail 6-5-17?
faq.a: The middle position N equals reduce(M+D): 6 + 17 = 23, then 2 + 3 = 5. That is why the calculator gives exactly the order 6-5-17. The arithmetic confirms the place of The Hierophant, and the article shows how it holds the choice between entry Lovers and root Star.

faq.q: Is this a “bad” trio for relationships?
faq.a: Not bad, just prone to spinning its wheels. The combination itself is rare and strong: a pull towards people, a sense of meaning and a high bar. What makes it heavy is not “evil fate” but the fact that a living desire passes through two filters at once — the rule and the ideal — and often never reaches a decision. When the filters stop arguing, the choice becomes conscious and deep.

Begin with one observation: catch the moment when you are drawn to someone or something, and notice what switches on right after it — “is this really how it should be” and “does it come up to the ideal”. That is the exact spot where the living desire is handed over to the rule and the dream for trial. After that, give it a voice back before the checking starts.
